summary.short: ACM decision amending the Dutch electricity Netcode, effective 1 October 2024, so that grid operators give transport-capacity priority in congestion areas to listed parties (congestion mitigators, safety functions and basic-needs providers) instead of first come, first served, subject to declarations and documents.
summary.long: The ACM decision of 12 April 2024 amends the Netcode elektriciteit under the Elektriciteitswet 1998 by adding Articles 7.0a to 7.0d and Annex 22. In congestion areas, grid operators must allocate transport capacity by priority category instead of first come, first served. Category 1 covers congestion mitigators that have a contract with the operator. Category 2 covers listed safety functions (fire services, ambulance posts, police, armed forces, intelligence services, NCTV, courts, prisons, water management and acute healthcare). Category 3 covers basic needs (public drinking water, compulsory education, housing up to 3x35A, heat and gas networks). Categories 2 and 3 apply to offtake only. Applicants must submit a board declaration and documents such as a recent Chamber of Commerce extract. Operators check complete requests within twenty working days, may suspend prioritisation in agreement with the ACM when more than 25% of requests in a quarter are priority requests, withdraw capacity for breach or fraud, and report annually by 31 March. The decision takes effect on 1 October 2024, and the ACM plans an evaluation within two years.](truncated)

notes: This is part 1 of 4 of the instrument; annotations cover the provisions shown here (Artikel I to II, Toelichting, and Bijlage 1 in part). Several Netcode references (artikelen 9.5, 9.6, 9.8, 9.9) are internal to the amended instrument and not coded as relations. Internal inconsistencies: (1) Netcode artikel 7.0a(8) counts the 25% trigger against all transport requests under artikel 24(1) E-wet, while randnummer 119 counts it against transport requests in the waiting list; (2) randnummer 146 repeats the same sentence on the Verordening Gasleveringszekerheid twice; (3) randnummer 124 and 125 say SBI codes will change in 2025, which is not reflected in the operative text. The Toelichting is context only; obligations and thresholds must be taken from Artikel I. This part covers paragraphs 1-182 of the ACM's response-to-comments annex, plus quoted statutory and EU texts. The decision's operative conditions, dates and sanctions are in other parts and are not annotated here. Relations to the Elektriciteitswet, Gaswet and Warmtewet are recorded as cross-references because they are quoted or cited in the text, not as enacted relations of this decision. Paragraph 30 refers to randnummer 328, which is outside this part. Several entries are named by reference to Annex 22 of the Netcode and to paragraph 6.1 of an explanatory memorandum, which are not included in this part. Part 3 of 4 (randnummers 183-532) is the ACM's response to consultation comments. Operative changes are described in the reasoning: categories 4a and 4b deleted (para 329); application made mandatory in congestion areas (para 456, 468); FCFS kept within categories (para 268); fraud clause for withdrawing capacity (art. 7.0c lid 2, para 443); duty to contact the ACM when more than 25% of queued transport requests are prioritisation requests (art. 7.0a lid 8, para 443); annual reporting (para 492); evaluation within two years of entry into force (para 494); entry into force 1 October 2024 (para 505). Legal basis of the decision (E-wet art. 31 lid 1 onder a juncto 32 lid 2) appears in the title and is not in this part. Naming variants: 'InVesta' (para 246) vs 'Stichting Investa' (para 271); 'Energy Board Provincie Utrecht' (para 257) vs 'Energyboard Utrecht' (para 296). Para 442 is a broken heading ('Conclusie 442.'). Opleidingsinstituut DJI is not included as a support service (para 281). Commenters who are not addressees are not listed as entities. Part 3 ends mid-section (para 532). Part 4 of 4 contains only the conclusion (randnummer 533) and footnotes 1 to 153; no operative provisions. Relations come from footnote citations and show what the decision relies on, applies or contrasts; the legal basis is not stated in this part. The footnotes repeat several notes (e.g., 17 and 121, 29 and 135, 49 and 115); both copies were treated as one source. Internal inconsistency: note 24 gives Staatsblad 2021, 291 for the Besluit of 15 June 2021, while note 129 gives Staatsblad 2012, 291. The text uses both 'groot algemeen belang' (note 29) and 'groot openbaar belang' (notes 1 and 36), although the conclusion refers to consistent terminology. The expansion of BHG is taken from note 31 and is not stated in this part.
